title: Rose and leaf pincushion
subtitle: A 10 cm round pincushion with a stylised rose motif in continental tent stitch on 13-count canvas
excerpt: A circular pincushion worked in continental tent stitch on 13-count canvas. The design centres on a five-petal rose in three shades of pink surrounded by four leaves. Finished size is 10 cm in diameter, stuffed firmly.
sourceNotes: Rose motif adapted from flower chart in Weldon's Practical Needlework, canvaswork series (1887). Beeton, Book of Needlework (1870), Project Gutenberg #16746, rose pattern chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: The technique of placing adjacent tent stitches in graduating shades of one colour to create the illusion of a curved or three-dimensional surface.

heroPrompt: A small round needlepoint pincushion with a pink rose and green leaf motif on a cream background, pins inserted at the edges, on a wooden sewing table, natural light.

content.text: This pincushion is a 52-hole circle on 13-count canvas, worked in continental tent stitch from the centre outward. The rose uses three shades of pink for
tent stitch shading
: a dark centre, medium petals, and pale outer edges. The four leaves use two shades of green. The background is cream throughout.
What you need

items.label: Thread: rose dark
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 3350 / Anchor 59 (ultra dark dusty rose). About 1 m

items.label: Thread: rose medium
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 3354 / Anchor 74 (light dusty rose). About 2 m

items.label: Thread: rose light
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 3716 / Anchor 25 (very light dusty rose). About 2 m

items.label: Thread: leaf dark
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 987 / Anchor 244 (dark forest green). About 1.5 m

items.label: Thread: leaf light
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 989 / Anchor 242 (forest green). About 1.5 m

items.label: Thread: background
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 712 / Anchor 926 (cream). About 5 m

content.text: Palette
Rose dark: DMC 3350 / Anchor 59: ultra dark dusty rose
Rose medium: DMC 3354 / Anchor 74: light dusty rose
Rose light: DMC 3716 / Anchor 25: very light dusty rose
Leaf dark: DMC 987 / Anchor 244: dark forest green
Leaf light: DMC 989 / Anchor 242: forest green
Background: DMC 712 / Anchor 926: cream
Stretching the canvas
Mount the canvas on a hoop or frame. Continental tent stitch distorts the canvas if worked in the hand; a frame keeps the circle round and the background fill straight.
Stitches used
Continental tent stitch
throughout.
Working method
Mark the centre hole of the canvas with a basting thread. This is the centre of the rose.
Work the rose centre: five or six stitches in the dark shade, forming the inner petals around the centre hole.
Work the medium rose shade around the dark centre, extending the petals outward.
Work the outer petal edges in the light rose shade. The three-shade shading gives the rose a rounded, slightly three-dimensional appearance.
Work the four leaf shapes, one at each diagonal from the rose. Use the leaf dark for the outer edges and the lighter shade for the centre vein area.
Fill the background in cream. The filled area is the 52-hole circle, so the background fill terminates where the circle edge falls. Use basketweave for the fill rows if possible to reduce distortion.
Block lightly by dampening and pressing between two towels under a book for a few hours.
Finishing

Cut the canvas into a circle, leaving a 1.5 cm margin outside the stitched edge. Run a gathering stitch through the margin. Place the stuffing ball in the centre, pull the gathering thread tight to gather the margin behind, and stitch to secure. Slip-stitch the felt circle to the back.
What to try next
A Victorian pansy or tulip motif uses the same three-shade shading technique and the same pincushion construction. Both appear in Weldon's charted patterns.
